page: Hetzner Cloud ccx13 is a dedicated CPU virtual server instance powered by the x86_64 AMD EPYC processor architecture. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with 2 threads per core, operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The instance is equipped with 8.0 GB of RAM, translating to 3.91 GB per core, and includes 80 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Virtualization is managed via the QEMU hypervisor, and the instance does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

In benchmark evaluations, the ccx13 demonstrates a clear divergence between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core performance is strong, with a stress-ng single-core score of 3074.79 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1970.0, both placing in the top 25% of tested servers. However, multi-core performance is limited, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 2523.0 and a stress-ng multi-core score of 3074.79, both falling into the bottom 25%. Memory performance is a notable bottleneck; the Passmark memory score and small-block read-only memory bandwidth of 150.52 GB/sec rank in the bottom 10%, though large-block write bandwidth remains average at 26.66 GB/sec.

The dedicated CPU allocation provides predictable execution times for single-threaded tasks, making it a cost-efficient entry point for workloads requiring dedicated resources without the overhead of shared-core steal time. However, database operations and high-throughput web serving are constrained, as evidenced by a poor Passmark database score of 989.94 and a weak static web serving throughput of 3.1 GB/sec. This instance is best suited for lightweight single-threaded applications, basic text processing, and small-scale LLM text generation using compact models, rather than memory-intensive databases or parallelized compilation tasks.
